message.content:
**Uno – Basic Rules (for a standard 108‑card deck)** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or play all your cards and win the round). Points are tallied at the end of each round. | | **Setup** | • Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card (Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Wild, or Wild Draw Four), follow its effect before play begins. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card from your hand if it matches the color, number, or symbol of the top card on the discard pile. You may also play:
• A **Wild** card (any color) or
• A **Wild Draw Four** (must be played only when no other playable card exists; otherwise you’re penalized). | | **Special Cards** | • **Draw Two (+2)** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Wild** – Player chooses the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – Same as Wild, but next player draws four cards and loses their turn. | | **Drawing a Card** | If you cannot play any card, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may immediately play it; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you have only one card left, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. Failure to do so results in a penalty: you must draw two cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points based on the cards remaining in opponents’ hands: numbers count as face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip +20, Wild/Wild Draw Four +50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches 500 points (or another agreed target). | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of what has been played** – helps you decide when to use Wild Draw Four strategically. 2. **Use Reverse wisely** – in a 2‑player game it acts like Skip. 3. **Watch your opponents’ colors** – if they’re low on a certain color, avoid playing that color. Enjoy the game!
